title: Inline type tests so the C compiler folds them
motivation: A type assumption such as `r ?: v(I)` compiled to `Fir_assume_type(r, Fir_type(Fir_kind_primitive_vector(1), ...))`. At run time that was five out-of-line calls: a table read, a struct build, `Fir_assume_type`, `Fir_value_matches`, and `Fir_value_kind_matches` with `Rf_length`. The needed test is one `TYPEOF` compare and one attribute test, sometimes with a length test. The cost showed most in the loop benchmarks with many type checks (`bench_simple_empty_while`, `bench_simple_bytecodes`, `bench_simple_scalar-while`, `sieve`).
solution: The type descriptors (`Fir_kind_*`, `Fir_promisity_*`, `Fir_type`, `Fir_signature`) and the value tests (`Fir_value_kind_matches`, `Fir_value_matches`, `Fir_assume_type`) move from `runtime.c` to `runtime.h` as `static ALWAYS_INLINE` functions and constant compound literals (C only). With constant arguments, the C compiler reduces a type assumption to a few loads and compares: the `TYPEOF` tag, the attributes, and sometimes the length. Only the promise slow path `Fir_promise_value_matches` stays out of line. The emitted C text does not change.

files.client/rsh/src/fir2c/runtime.c: Removes the type descriptor globals and constructors and the value type tests, and exports `Fir_promise_value_matches` as the slow path.
files.client/rsh/src/fir2c/runtime.h: Defines the type descriptors and the value type tests as `static ALWAYS_INLINE` functions and compound-literal macros, for C only.
